title: Point of Interest
description:
An authored place inside a field map -- a shrine, a fossil cliff, a river house. The generator never invents these; it lays terrain and the adapter places them on it, which is what keeps Garudasaur's Ledge a specific place rather than a random cave.

Deep locations do not get their own entity type. A point of interest that can be entered carries `sub_locations`, so Garudasaur's Ledge is one record listing its cliff, moss cavern, nest and bone field rather than five records and a container.

kind.description: What sort of place it is. Drives how the diary files what is found here, and which discipline gains from documenting it.

stands.description:
Whether this place wants height, as distinct from a biome. `terrain` says what the ground is made of; this says where it sits on the slope, which is a different question and was not askable before. A watch stair wants somewhere you can see from; a drowned dockyard is underwater by definition. `either` is the honest default and most places mean it -- a midden is wherever the city put it.

Read against the generator's three elevation terraces, the same ones cliffs are drawn between: `high` prefers band 1 or 2, `low` prefers band 0. A preference rather than a rule -- a map with no high ground still has to put the place somewhere, and refusing would lose it entirely.
stands.$comment: Added when every point of interest on Lothal and Dwarka was landing on band 0 while both maps carried over a hundred and twenty hill tiles. Nothing was choosing badly: no place on either map listed `hills` in its terrain, so high ground was never a candidate. Canon was right about the biomes -- a silted granary and a tide market are low by their own description -- so the fix was a word for the thing canon could not say.

terrain.description: Which of the field map's biomes this can be placed on. The adapter needs somewhere plausible to put it.

sub_locations.description: Named places within this one, for a point of interest deep enough to be entered rather than merely visited. An empty or absent list means it is explored where it stands.

requires.description: Discovery or vocabulary ids that must be held before this can be reached. This is how a cave that is 'too dark' opens later.

npcs.description: npc ids who can be met here.

related_entities.description: Any canon ids this place is about -- a settlement, an event, a character, a species. This is what makes a place mean something rather than merely exist.

description.description: What the player sees on approach.

arrival.description: Longer prose for stepping inside. Player-facing.

notes.description: Reference fact for the canon reader.

ruin_of.description: The entity this place used to be, when it is now a wreck of it. Lothal in Epoch 5 is `kind: settlement` with `ruin_of: settlement_lothal` -- survivors camped inside the half-buried relic, so it is a living place and a ruin at once rather than either. Lets the diary say what stood here without duplicating the entity.
